You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: Where should I create an issue for onboarding, offboarding, or transition questions?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): In the Employment Issue Tracker subproject.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[People Group > Welcome > Connect with us]
- [**The People Group**](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-ops) holds several subprojects to organize the people group; please create an issue in the appropriate subproject or `general` if you're not sure. Please use confidential issues for topics that should only be visible to GitLab team-members. Similarly, if your question can be shared please use a public issue. Tag `@gl-people-ops-team` or `@gl-hiring` so the appropriate team members can follow up.
  - Please note that not all People Group projects can be shared in an issue due to confidentiality. When we cannot be completely transparent, we will share what we can in the issue description, and explain why.
  - [**Employment Issue Tracker**](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/people-operations/employment-templates): Only Onboarding, Offboarding and Transition Issue Templates are held in this subproject, and they are created by the People Operations Team only. Interview Training Issues, are held in the [Training project](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/Training) and created by the Talent Acquisition team. Please see the [interviewing page](/handbook/hiring/interviewing) for more info.
- **People Operations**; Please create a case for the People Operations team with any questions that do not seem appropriate for the issue tracker within [Compass](/handbook/eta/corporate-it/compass/compass-guide/#how-to-get-help-3-ways-to-reach-compass) - choosing the applicable template/category applicable. For access 

[GitLab Offboarding FAQ > Timing > When will my offboarding issue be created?]
Offboarding issues are used for de-provisioning purposes so you, as the team member, do not need to do anything to get it opened or will have any action items within the issue.

The People Operations Team member assigned to your offboarding will ensure the automation triggers to create the offboarding issue on the last working day by 4pm (local time) Monday-Friday.

[GitLab Internal Acceptable Use Policy > Purpose > Procedure > Consultations]
To consult with the Security Team create an issue in the [Security Compliance tracker](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/gl-security/security-assurance/team-commercial-compliance/compliance/issues).

Exceptions to this policy must be approved by Security, Legal and PeopleOps Departments.

- [Onboarding Issue](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/people-operations/employment-templates/-/blob/main/.gitlab/issue_templates/onboarding.md)
- [Data Classification Standard](/handbook/security/policies_and_standards/data-classification-standard/)
- [Asset return procedure](/handbook/people-group/offboarding/#returning-property-to-gitlab)
- [Lost or stolen asset procedure](/handbook/security#reporting-an-incident)
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
Based on the context provided, you should create an issue in the **Employment Issue Tracker** subproject (specifically at `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/people-operations/employment-templates`).

However, please note that these issues (Onboarding, Offboarding, and Transition) are **created by the People Operations Team only**. If you have questions regarding these processes that do not fit into an issue, you should create a case for the People Operations team via **Compass**.
"""

Grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
Return JSON: {"correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false, "reason": "one sentence"}
